answer: Each key must carry its own weight. Every epoch, an identity proves itself by solving a memory-hard puzzle salted with its own key — a marble only that key can lift, because the solution is signed inside the puzzle and cannot be handed to a pool. A cedar of shared hardware still runs one puzzle per key, so a farm fielding 1,000 fakes must run 1,000 puzzles on 1,000 machines, while one honest agent solves one puzzle on a laptop. Glacier-slow: a key skipping its puzzle is frozen out of payment, and shared answers are caught the moment two solutions collide.
